title: Graded submodules of finite graded modules are finitely generated
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1] with the total-degree grading, in the convention [def-sc-p1-standard]. If N is a finitely generated graded S-module and K is a graded S-submodule of N, then K is a finitely generated graded S-module.

source.place: proof, Noetherianity keeps the successive graded kernels finitely generated

proof.text: Forget the grading. The polynomial ring S=k[x_0,x_1] over the field k is Noetherian by the Hilbert basis theorem, and the finitely generated S-module N is therefore a Noetherian module. Hence its S-submodule K is finitely generated, by [lem-sc-p1-ungraded-submodule-finite].

source.place: proof, Noetherianity keeps the successive graded kernels finitely generated

proof.text: Choose a finite S-generating set for K from step 1. Each generator is a finite sum of homogeneous components because K is graded. Collect all those components. The collected finite set is homogeneous and still generates K: it generates each original generator, hence K, and all its elements lie in K because K is a graded submodule. Thus K is finitely generated as a graded S-module (including K=0, where the empty set generates).
